subject.title: fix(pairing): preserve authorized senders when allowFrom reads fail

question: Should maintainers repair this current upstream branch or replace it with a clean narrow pairing-fix branch before any merge attempt?
rationale: The core bug fix is valuable, but the current head is conflicting, uneditable through maintainerCanModify=false, and includes unrelated security/automation/dependency/runtime changes that require human ownership before merge.

options.title: Narrow and repair this branch
options.body: Preserve the pairing commits, remove unrelated current-head drift, fix malformed JSON fail-closed handling, resolve conflicts, and rerun exact-head proof.

options.title: Open a clean replacement
options.body: Create a new narrow PR from current main that credits this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98313 while leaving this branch unmerged.

options.title: Intentionally split unrelated work
options.body: If the large native-i18n/workflow/dependency changes are desired, separate them into owned PRs with their own proof and security review.

recommendation.title: Narrow and repair this branch
recommendation.body: Preserve the pairing commits, remove unrelated current-head drift, fix malformed JSON fail-closed handling, resolve conflicts, and rerun exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored and owns the upstream branch and has prior pairing/allowlist history, so he is the best available routing owner for branch repair or replacement.
